To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SNARE proteins syntaxin, SNAP-25, and synaptobrevin (VAMP) are assembled in the presynaptic bouton of cultured hippocampal neurons and undergo rapid rearrangements in the resting state and on exocytotic fusion of vesicles with the plasma membrane.

FRET and fluorescence lifetime imaging of SNAREs in cultured hippocampal neurons revealed that SNAREs are assembled at resting synapses, disassembled after exocytosis and reassembled at newly docked synaptic vesicles.

SNARE proteins are present in the active zone as preassembled complexes, undergo conformational changes on exocytotic fusion, and are disassembled in the periphery and reassembled on newly docked vesicle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of neurotransmission and the dynamics of SNARE proteins at the presynaptic terminal.
the molecular mechanisms of synaptic transmission, the fundamental process of information storage and retrieval.
the spatiotemporel dynamics of SNAREs and their partners during synaptic vesicle fusion, endocytosis, and recycling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SNAREs are assembled and rearranged on a rapid time scale in a complex manner in the active zone.
SNAREs are present in docked synaptic vesicles, and their assembly and conformational rearrangements can be monitored with FRET in living neurons.
the FRET measurements in this study are a major advance in the field of SNARE function, and the data are consistent with the current models of SNARE dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FRET can detect the assembly and disassembly of small numbers of SNAREs in a subcellular compartment, the presynaptic active zone, and the rearrangement of SNAREs during exocytosis.
FRET and fluorescence lifetime imaging of SNARE proteins in living neurons provides a powerful new approach for the study of SNARE dynamics in the context of synaptic transmission.

we have used FRET and fluorescence lifetime imaging to detect the assembly, disassembly, and reassembly of the SNARE complex in the active zone, the reorientation of the complex on vesicle fusion, and the dispersal of the complex after fusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SNARE complex is a dynamic molecular machine that undergoes conformational changes, disassembly, and reassembly during the exo/endocytotic cycle.
FRET and lifetime imaging microscopy are powerful tools to study SNARE dynamics at synapses.
FRET can be used to detect SNARE rearrangements and assembly at neuronal synapses.
